faq_complete_provider_explanation.message: completeProvider: true blocks every request the provider matches, before any rule runs. Blocking only happens while "Allow domain blocking" is on in Settings. In a remote rule list, it also waits until you approve that list's block capability in Remote Rules Health.

faq_custom_rules_note.message: Custom rules are applied last. A custom provider replaces every built-in or remote provider with the same domainPatterns or urlPattern; their rules are not combined. Other custom providers are added alongside them.

faq_domain_pattern_basic.message: example.com - URLs that contain this text anywhere, which can also be inside a longer host name or path

faq_domain_pattern_tld.message: ||example.*^ - example on any public suffix, including multi-part ones (example.de, example.co.uk)

faq_domain_pattern_wildcard.message: *.example.com - also a contains match, with * as a wildcard; use ||example.com^ for a domain

faq_domain_patterns_explanation.message: domainPatterns is a list of AdBlock-style patterns. A URL matches if any of them matches. Public suffixes are handled correctly, so ||example.*^ also covers example.co.uk:

faq_exceptions_explanation.message: Exceptions list URLs the provider leaves alone. Each entry is a regex for the full URL (for example ^https?:\/\/example\.com\/login) or a domain pattern starting with | (for example ||example.com^/login). If a URL matches, none of the provider's rules run.

faq_exceptions_usage.message: Use exceptions to protect login pages, API endpoints or other URLs that break when cleaned. To skip one rule instead of the whole provider, give that rule its own exceptions.

faq_force_redirection_explanation.message: Normally a redirect only changes the network request. With forceRedirection: true, a redirect on a page load (main_frame) makes the whole tab navigate to the new address.

faq_force_redirection_usage.message: Use it when a site's redirect page doesn't follow a normal redirect, so the tab would otherwise stay on the tracking page.

faq_force_redirection_warning.message: Only use it when normal redirections don't work, because it navigates the tab directly.

faq_history_bypass_protection_explanatio.message: Single-page sites often change the address with history.pushState/replaceState instead of loading a new page. Linkumori cleans those addresses too. Add history-bypass-protection=false to a $removeparam filter to skip just that filter for these in-page changes; it still runs on normal requests.

faq_history_bypass_protection_provider.message: To skip a whole provider for in-page changes, set it on the provider:

faq_history_bypass_protection_default.message: Left out, it is true and in-page changes are cleaned. A rule's own setting beats the provider's, so a rule can opt back in with history-bypass-protection=true, or "historyBypassProtection": true in a rule object.

faq_index_pattern_explanation.message: indexPattern is a lookup hint for a provider that uses urlPattern, not a match condition. It lists hosts as domain patterns such as ||example.com^, so the provider is only checked for URLs on those hosts. The URL must still match urlPattern. It only works together with urlPattern.

faq_http_methods_explanation.message: methods limits a provider to some HTTP methods, such as ["GET"]. A $removeparam filter can do the same with a modifier such as method=get|~post.

faq_http_methods_post.message: POST - Form submissions and API calls

faq_http_methods_tip.message: Leave methods out to handle every method.

faq_provider_import_explanation.message: "Import/Disable Providers" lets you browse the providers of the built-in and remote rules. Import the ones you pick as custom rules to edit them, or disable providers you don't want.

faq_provider_import_tip.message: You can select several providers and import or disable them at once. "Disabled Rules" lists what you disabled and lets you restore it.

faq_provider_list.message: How do I manage my providers efficiently?

faq_provider_list_explanation.message: When no provider is open, the editor shows All Providers, a list of your custom providers. You can search, edit, duplicate or delete providers without opening each one.

faq_provider_list_tip.message: Close the open provider to return to the list.

faq_providers_explanation.message: A provider is a named group of rules for some URLs. domainPatterns or urlPattern decides which URLs it handles. The provider name is only a label and does not affect matching.

faq_raw_rules_explanation.message: Each entry is a regular expression run on the whole URL; every match is deleted. Raw rules always run before rules.

faq_raw_rules_usage.message: Use rawRules for text that isn't a name=value parameter, such as a /ref=… path segment. Any entry in either list can also be a rule object with matchPattern and optional id, replacePattern, order and more.

faq_redirections_explanation.message: Redirections send the request somewhere else. A regex entry redirects to its capture group, so it needs exactly one ( … ). An entry starting with | is a fixed redirect: "||go.example.com^$redirect=https://example.com/" sends every matching URL to that address. Redirects only run while "Enable Third-Party Redirect Bypass" is on in Settings (off by default).

faq_redirections_process.message: The captured value is URL-decoded and must be an absolute http or https address; otherwise nothing is redirected and the provider's other rules run. fieldRedirections redirects to a parameter's value without a regex. In a remote rule list, redirects wait until you approve that list's redirect capability.

faq_referral_default.message: "Allow referral marketing" is off by default, so these parameters are removed unless the user turns it on.

faq_referral_explanation.message: referralMarketing takes the same entries as rules, for affiliate and referral parameters that support creators and shops. They are removed only while "Allow referral marketing" is off in Settings. A rule in rules can count as referral marketing with "referralMarketing": true.

faq_resource_types_explanation.message: resourceTypes limits a provider to some request types (pages, frames, scripts, images and so on). A rule object can do the same with requestTypes, and a $removeparam filter with modifiers such as document or xmlhttprequest.

faq_resource_types_tip.message: Leave it out to handle every request type. There is no request type list in Settings; request types come only from the rules.

faq_rt_object_subrequest.message: object_subrequest - Requests made by embedded objects

faq_rt_other.message: other - Other types not covered above

faq_rules_converted.message: Example: "utm_source" removes exactly that parameter; "utm_.*" removes utm_source, utm_campaign and so on. Names and regexes run first, then $removeparam filters, except where an @@ entry keeps the parameter.

faq_rules_explanation.message: Each entry removes matching parameters from the query (?a=1) and the fragment (#a=1). An entry is a parameter name, a regex for the whole name, or a $removeparam filter, optionally with a pattern in front such as ||example.com^$removeparam=tag.

faq_url_pattern_explanation.message: urlPattern is one regular expression, tested case-insensitively against the full URL, that decides which URLs the provider handles. Use it or domainPatterns, never both. Add indexPattern so the provider is only checked on matching hosts instead of against every URL.

faq_url_pattern_structure.message: A typical urlPattern covers the scheme, any subdomains, the domain and, when needed, the start of the path.

faq_url_pattern_tip.message: In JSON, write each backslash twice. Test the regex before saving; the editor rejects invalid ones.

faq_url_patterns_explanation.message: urlPattern is one regular expression for the full URL, for matches that domain patterns can't express:

faq_use_domain_patterns.message: Use domainPatterns for sites and paths. It is simpler, and it lets the provider be found by host name.

faq_use_url_patterns.message: Use urlPattern only when you need a regular expression, and add indexPattern with it.

audit_faq_intro.message: These notes describe the provider fields of CLN Format 1.0, the rule format Linkumori reads.

audit_faq_audit_provider_title.message: How do I audit a provider?

audit_faq_audit_provider_body.message:
Open a source in the viewer, find the provider inside providers, and inspect the keys on that provider object.

Use Bundled Rules to inspect the shipped rules, Final Rules to inspect the merged runtime result, Custom Rules to inspect user overrides, and Latest Cached Remote Rules to inspect the most recently fetched remote payload saved in cache.

audit_faq_override_title.message: How do I enable, disable, import, edit, or override individual rules?

audit_faq_override_body.message:
Use the Custom Rules Editor for rule-by-rule control. There you can import a built-in or remote provider as a custom rule, edit it, switch single rules off, or disable whole providers.

A custom provider replaces every built-in or remote provider with the same domainPatterns or urlPattern; their rules are not combined.

Audit Bundled Rules or Latest Cached Remote Rules to find the provider you want, then check Custom Rules and Final Rules to confirm your change takes effect.

audit_faq_url_pattern_body.message:
urlPattern is one regular expression, tested case-insensitively against the full URL, that decides which URLs the provider handles.

A provider has urlPattern or domainPatterns, never both. indexPattern lists the hosts a urlPattern provider is checked on, so it isn't tested against every URL.

audit_faq_domain_patterns_body.message:
domainPatterns lists AdBlock-style patterns such as ||example.com^ (the domain and its subdomains) or ||example.*^ (any public suffix). A URL matches if any of them matches.

Use it or urlPattern, never both. Domain patterns let the provider be found by host name, so they are faster than a regex.

audit_faq_rules_title.message: What can rules, rawRules and referralMarketing contain?

audit_faq_rules_body.message:
rules entries are parameter names, name regexes, $removeparam filters, or rule objects with matchPattern and optional id, replacePattern, order and more.

rawRules entries are regular expressions run on the whole URL; every match is deleted. They always run before rules.

referralMarketing takes the same entries as rules, but only runs while referral marketing is not allowed. A rules object can do the same with "referralMarketing": true.

audit_faq_exceptions_body.message:
exceptions lists URLs the provider leaves alone. Each entry is a regular expression, or a domain pattern that starts with |, such as ||example.com^/login.

If one matches, none of the provider's rules run, even though the provider matched. To keep a single parameter instead, use an @@ entry in rules.

audit_faq_redirections_body.message:
redirections entries are regular expressions with exactly one capture group, whose URL-decoded value becomes the new address, or fixed redirects such as ||go.example.com^$redirect=https://example.com/.

fieldRedirections names a parameter whose value becomes the new address.

A redirect only happens to an absolute http or https address, and only while Third-Party Redirect Bypass is on. In a remote rule list it also waits for that list's redirect approval in Remote Rules Health.

audit_faq_methods_resources_body.message:
methods restricts a provider to HTTP methods such as GET or POST. If none are listed, every method is handled.

resourceTypes restricts a provider to request types such as main_frame, sub_frame or xmlhttprequest. If none are listed, every request type is handled.

Single rules can be limited with requestTypes, directly or through the file's defaults. There is no request type list in Settings.

audit_faq_complete_force_body.message:
completeProvider: true blocks every matching request before any rule runs, while domain blocking is allowed in Settings.

forceRedirection: true makes a redirect on a page load (main_frame) navigate the whole tab instead of only the network request.

In a remote rule list, both wait until you approve that list's block or redirect capability in Remote Rules Health.

audit_faq_fields_body.message:
A provider can have: domainPatterns, urlPattern, indexPattern, rules, referralMarketing, rawRules, exceptions, redirections, fieldRedirections, completeProvider, forceRedirection, methods, resourceTypes, historyBypassProtection and active.

Besides providers, a rule file can have cln (the format version, "1.0"), metadata, defaults and, in a remote rule list, patches.

When auditing behavior, check Final Rules first: it shows the result after built-in, remote and custom rules are combined and patches are applied.

guide_intro_p_1.message: Linkumori cleans URLs with rules written in CLN Format 1.0 (Clean Link Notation), a JSON format. This guide goes from a first rule to every option, with examples you can copy.

guide_intro_p_2.message: The built-in rules, remote rule lists and your custom rules all use the same format. You write custom rules in the custom rules editor, which checks them when you save or import. An official ClearURLs rule catalog (data.min.json) is already a valid CLN file and can be used as it is.

guide_file_p1.message: A rules file is one JSON object. Its providers object maps a name of your choice to a provider:

guide_file_p2.message: A provider says which URLs it handles and what to do with them. This one removes utm_source and utm_medium from every URL on example.com and its subdomains:

guide_rules_file_p_1.message: The provider name is only a label. Which URLs a provider handles is decided by domainPatterns or urlPattern.

guide_rules_file_cell_2.message: Optional format version. The only valid value is "1.0". A file without it is read as 1.0 too; any other value rejects the file. It is not called version because the ClearURLs new rule format already uses that key.

guide_rules_file_cell_4.message: Values for every rule of the file that doesn't set its own (chapter 12).

guide_rules_file_cell_5.message: Remote rule lists only: replacements for rules that are already loaded (chapter 15).

guide_provider_fields_cell_1.message: Which URLs the provider handles, as one domain pattern or a list of them (chapter 3). Use this or urlPattern, never both.

guide_provider_fields_cell_2.message: Which URLs the provider handles, as one regular expression matched against the full URL. Case is ignored.

guide_provider_fields_cell_3.message: Only with urlPattern: host hints such as ||example.com^, so the provider is only checked for those hosts instead of against every URL. It is a lookup hint, not a match condition.

guide_provider_fields_cell_4.message: Referral and affiliate parameters to remove. Skipped while Allow referral marketing is on (chapter 10).

guide_field_rawrules.message: Regular expressions run on the full URL; every match is deleted (chapter 6).

guide_provider_fields_cell_5.message: URLs the provider leaves completely alone (chapter 7).

guide_provider_fields_cell_6.message: Send the request to another address instead of editing it (chapter 8).

guide_provider_fields_cell_7.message: Send the request to the value of a parameter (chapter 8).

guide_field_completeprovider.message: true blocks every request the provider matches, while Allow domain blocking is on.

guide_provider_fields_cell_8.message: true: when a page load (main_frame) is redirected, the whole tab navigates to the new address, not just the network request.

guide_provider_fields_cell_9.message: Only handle these HTTP methods, for example ["GET"]. Left out: every method.

guide_provider_fields_cell_10.message: Only handle these request types, for example ["main_frame", "xmlhttprequest"]. Left out: every request type.

guide_provider_fields_cell_11.message: Default true. false skips the whole provider when a page changes its own address with the History API (pushState/replaceState). Normal network requests are still cleaned.

guide_provider_fields_cell_12.message: false switches the provider off without deleting it.

guide_matching_p_1.message: domainPatterns is a list of domain patterns. A URL matches if any of them matches. The same patterns are used in front of exceptions, redirections, $removeparam filters and raw rules.

guide_pat_path.message: that host and its subdomains, when the path starts with /path

guide_pat_start.message: URLs that start with exactly this text

guide_pat_end.message: URLs that end with exactly this text

guide_matching_cell_1.message: the full URL, as a regular expression

guide_matching_cell_2.message: URLs that contain this text anywhere (no leading |)

guide_matching_p_2.message: ^ marks the end of the host name, or a separator such as /, ?, : or the end of the URL. * is a wildcard.

guide_matching_p_3.message: || stands for a domain: the host and every subdomain. A single | stands for the very start of the URL and must be followed by a scheme such as https://. For a domain you always want ||; |example.com^ can never match, so the editor rejects it.

guide_matching_p_4.message: For example, ||smile.amazon.*^ reads as: || the host and its subdomains, smile.amazon the required labels, .* any public suffix (.com, .co.jp, .de, …), and ^ the end of the host.

guide_match_p4.message: To match with a regular expression instead, use urlPattern, and add indexPattern so the provider is only checked on those hosts:

guide_match_p5.message: A provider has domainPatterns or urlPattern, never both. If you need both kinds of match, make two providers.

guide_rules_p1.message: Each entry in rules removes parameters from the query (?a=1) and from the fragment (#a=1). An entry is one of:

guide_removing_parameters_cell_2.message: every parameter whose whole name matches; case is ignored

guide_removing_parameters_p_1.message: "fbclid" and "$removeparam=fbclid" remove the same thing. Use the plain name unless you need something from chapter 5. Any entry can also be written as a rule object (chapter 9).

guide_rules_part_title.message: Rules for part of a provider

guide_rules_p3.message: A plain name applies to every URL the provider matches. To remove a parameter on only some of them, put a pattern in front of a $removeparam filter:

guide_removing_parameters_p_2.message: Here qid is removed on every Amazon site, tag only on amazon.de, sr only on smile.amazon, and ref_ only under /gp/. The pattern narrows the provider's own patterns; it can never widen them.

guide_rp_p1.message: A $removeparam filter has this shape; the parts in brackets are optional:

guide_removeparam_filters_item_1.message: @@ turns the filter into an exception that keeps the parameter (see below).

guide_removeparam_filters_item_2.message: pattern narrows the filter to some of the provider's URLs (chapter 3). Left out, it applies to every URL the provider matches.

guide_removeparam_filters_item_3.message: =value picks the parameters. Left out, every parameter is removed.

guide_removeparam_filters_item_4.message: Modifiers say when the filter fires. Every modifier listed must hold; there is no "or" between them.

guide_rp_p2.message: The first character of the value decides what it means:

guide_removeparam_filters_cell_2.message: parameters whose name, or name=value together, matches the regular expression; add i to ignore case

guide_rp_v_name.message: exactly that parameter; case is ignored unless you add match-case

guide_removeparam_filters_p_1.message: A backslash makes the next character literal, so any parameter name can be targeted:

guide_removeparam_filters_p_2.message: These five are the only escapes in a name value; a backslash before any other character is an error. Inside a /regex/ value the backslash keeps its regex meaning. The escapes work in rules, referralMarketing, fieldRedirections and @@ entries. In JSON, write each backslash twice: "$removeparam=\\~foo".

guide_removeparam_filters_p_3.message: Modifiers come after the value, separated by commas. Separate several values of one modifier with |, and put ~ in front of a value to exclude it:

guide_removeparam_filters_cell_5.message: only when the page that made the request is (or, with ~, is not) one of these; regex values are allowed

guide_removeparam_filters_cell_6.message: only when the request itself goes to one of these, whatever page made it

guide_removeparam_filters_cell_8.message: only when the request goes to the same registrable domain as the page (a.example.com and b.example.com count as the same), or to a different one

guide_removeparam_filters_cell_9.message: the same, but comparing the exact host name, so a subdomain counts as third-party

guide_rp_o_types.message: only for these request types; ~type excludes one

guide_removeparam_filters_cell_11.message: skip this filter when a page changes its own address with the History API. Also accepts true/false, 1/0, yes/no

guide_removeparam_filters_p_4.message: The four *-party modifiers can't be combined with each other; first-party,third-party is rejected.

guide_removeparam_filters_p_5.message: For example, ||example.com^$removeparam=sid,domain=~partner.com,method=get,third-party removes sid on example.com, only for GET requests made by a page on another site, and never when that page is partner.com.

guide_rp_p5.message: A filter that starts with @@ keeps the parameter instead of removing it. Here ref is removed everywhere except on GitHub:

guide_removeparam_filters_item_5.message: An @@ entry only protects against $removeparam filters. A plain entry such as "ref" still removes the parameter; use a rule object's exceptions for that. Raw rules have their own @@…$rawrule= entries (chapter 6).

guide_removeparam_filters_item_6.message: Where you list it doesn't matter, and it can't have an order.

guide_removeparam_filters_item_7.message: Its pattern is checked against the URL as the provider received it, before raw rules run. An @@ entry scoped to a path that a raw rule deletes still matches.

guide_removeparam_filters_item_8.message: It also covers other providers' filters for requests made by a page this provider matches, which is handy for carving one site out of a rule defined elsewhere.

guide_raw_p1.message: A raw rule is a regular expression run on the full URL; every match is deleted. Use it for text that is not a name=value parameter, such as Amazon's /ref=… path segment:

guide_raw_rules_p_1.message: Raw rules run before rules, ignore case and replace every match (flags gi, or g with match-case). In JSON, write each backslash twice.

guide_raw_rules_p_2.message: A raw rule can take the pattern and modifiers of a $removeparam filter, with rawrule= last. Everything after rawrule= is the regular expression:

guide_raw_rules_p_3.message: The pattern and modifiers decide where the rule runs; the regular expression is still what gets deleted.

guide_raw_stop_title.message: Stopping raw rules on some URLs

guide_raw_rules_p_4.message: An entry that starts with @@ and ends in rawrule= keeps raw rules from running where its pattern matches:

guide_raw_rules_item_1.message: With nothing after rawrule=, it stops every raw rule of the provider on those URLs.

guide_raw_rules_item_2.message: With a regular expression after rawrule=, it stops the raw rules with that regular expression.

guide_raw_rules_item_3.message: As a rule object with targetId, it stops only the raw rule with that id or alias.

guide_raw_rules_p_5.message: To skip the whole provider, use exceptions instead.

guide_exceptions_p_1.message: If a URL matches an entry in exceptions, none of the provider's rules run for that request. An entry is a regular expression against the full URL, or a domain pattern that starts with |:

guide_exceptions_p_2.message: Exceptions ignore case. To skip a single rule instead of the whole provider, give that rule its own exceptions (chapter 9).

guide_redir_p1.message: Redirect rules skip tracking pages by going straight to the real destination. They only run while Enable Third-Party Redirect Bypass is on.

guide_redir_regex_title.message: Redirect to part of the URL

guide_redir_p2.message: An entry in redirections is a regular expression with exactly one capture group, ( … ). The request goes to what the group captured, URL-decoded. Write any other group as (?: … ):

guide_redir_p3.message: An entry that starts with | sends every matching URL to one address:

guide_redir_p4.message: fieldRedirections names the parameter that holds the destination, so no regular expression is needed. It takes the same entries as rules:

guide_redirects_p_1.message: Whichever matching parameter comes first in the URL wins. For https://site.example/away?redirect=https://real.example/page, the request goes to https://real.example/page.

guide_redirects_p_2.message: A redirect only happens to an absolute http or https address with a host. This is checked after preprocessors and percent-decoding. An invalid target makes the entry count as not matching: nothing is redirected, and the provider's later steps run on the unchanged URL.

guide_redirects_cell_3.message: no: the scheme is not http or https

guide_redirects_p_3.message: A raw rule whose result has a different scheme, host or port than its input counts as a redirect too, even when it only deletes text: deleting secure- from https://secure-bank.example/ lands on another site. It needs a valid target, and in a remote rule list the redirect approval (chapter 15). Otherwise the rule leaves the URL as it was.

guide_rule_objects_p_1.message: Any entry, in any list, can be an object instead of a string. Use one when a rule needs a stable id, should start switched off, should rewrite instead of remove, or should only run in some cases:

guide_rule_objects_cell_1.message: Required. The text you would write as a plain entry in that list.

guide_rule_objects_cell_2.message: A stable name (letters, digits, -, _) used to switch the rule on and off (chapter 14).

guide_rule_objects_cell_3.message: The rule's previous ids, so a setting saved under an old id keeps applying after a rename.

guide_rule_objects_cell_4.message: Rewrite instead of remove; §1§, §2§, … are the captured values.

guide_rule_objects_cell_6.message: Only for these request types, for example ["main_frame"]. Cleaning without a request (Copy clean link, the cleaning tool, History API changes) counts as main_frame.

guide_rule_objects_cell_7.message: URLs (regular expressions) where this one rule does not run.

guide_rule_objects_cell_8.message: Regular expression flags, as a string. Default i; in rawRules, gi (or g with match-case).

guide_rule_objects_cell_9.message: Run the rule earlier or later within its stage (chapter 13).

guide_rule_objects_cell_10.message: true: a rule in rules also counts as a referral-marketing rule (chapter 10).

guide_rule_objects_cell_11.message: The provider switch of the same name, for this one rule. It beats the provider's value and the file default.

guide_rule_objects_cell_13.message: A note for people reading the file; it must be a string.

guide_rule_objects_cell_14.message: Only on @@…$rawrule= entries: the id of the raw rule it stops.

guide_obj_p2.message: With replacePattern, a rule in rules keeps the parameter and replaces its value, which is §1§. In rawRules and redirections, §1§, §2§, … are the capture groups:

guide_rule_objects_p_2.message: Here ?token=abc123 becomes ?token=clean-abc123. A rewrite applies at most once per request, so it doesn't keep wrapping the value.

guide_rule_objects_p_3.message: Preprocessors change captured values, in order, before replacePattern or a redirect uses them. inputs is "all" or a list of group numbers:

guide_referral_marketing_p_1.message: referralMarketing takes the same entries as rules. They only run while Allow referral marketing is off, so affiliate links keep working if you turn it on:

guide_referral_marketing_p_2.message: A rule can stay in rules and still count as referral marketing, with "referralMarketing": true. Don't put the same text in both rules and referralMarketing; the editor warns about it.

guide_req_p1.message: These narrow down when a provider or a rule runs:

guide_request_types_cell_1.message: request types one rule object handles (also settable in defaults)

guide_req_options.message: the same for one $removeparam filter or raw rule

guide_request_types_p_1.message: Request types use the browser's names: main_frame (a page), sub_frame (a frame), xmlhttprequest, script, image and so on. Filter modifiers call the first two document and subdocument.

guide_request_types_p_2.message: Request types come only from the rules: there is no request type list in Settings. With none of these set, a rule cleans every request type.

guide_defaults_p_1.message: A top-level defaults block gives every rule of the file values it doesn't set itself:

guide_defaults_cell_1.message: active; false switches every rule off unless it says "active": true

guide_defaults_cell_2.message: requestTypes; "all" or leaving it out means every type

guide_defaults_item_1.message: A rule's own value always wins, and a rule's exceptions replace the default list instead of adding to it.

guide_defaults_item_2.message: Defaults apply to rules, rawRules, referralMarketing, redirections and fieldRedirections. A provider's own exceptions list is left alone. $redirect= entries only use active.

guide_defaults_item_3.message: Each file keeps its own defaults: the built-in rules, each remote list and your custom rules, also when overload mode merges them.

guide_defaults_item_4.message: For a completeProvider, the default requestTypes and exceptions also limit the block.

guide_defaults_item_5.message: Unknown keys and wrong types are errors, and a remote list with an invalid defaults block is rejected.

guide_defaults_p_2.message: In the custom rules editor, Manage rule defaults opens a form where you set a defaults block of your own and choose where it replaces the files' own:

guide_defaults_item_6.message: Each source's own (the default): every file uses its own defaults.

guide_defaults_item_7.message: Yours for built-in and remote rules: built-in and remote rules use yours; custom rules keep their own.

guide_defaults_item_8.message: Yours for all rules: every rule uses yours.

guide_defaults_p_3.message: The same form can edit the defaults of the built-in rules and of each loaded remote list. Your edit is stored in the extension, not in the file, and Reset to the file's defaults drops it. Merge from sources… combines the defaults of the sources you tick; nothing is stored until you save.

guide_order_p1.message: For each provider that matches the URL and allows the request:

guide_order_1.message: exceptions: if one matches, the provider is skipped.

guide_processing_order_item_1.message: redirections, then fieldRedirections: a match with a valid target redirects the request.

guide_processing_order_item_3.message: $removeparam filters run, except where an @@ entry keeps the parameter.

guide_processing_order_p_1.message: The first provider that changes, redirects or blocks the URL wins. The new URL then goes through the same steps again (see When processing stops).

guide_processing_order_p_2.message: Steps 4 and 5 are sorted together, by these rules in turn:

guide_processing_order_item_4.message: Raw rules always run first. No order moves a rules entry ahead of a raw rule. A cleanup that must happen before a raw rule has to be a raw rule itself.

guide_processing_order_item_5.message: Inside a stage, rules with order run before rules without one, lowest first. Negative numbers and fractions are allowed. order: 10 doesn't mean "tenth": it means after the stage's ordered rules below 10 and before all its unordered rules.

guide_processing_order_item_6.message: Then by list: rules, then rules objects marked "referralMarketing": true, then referralMarketing.

guide_processing_order_item_7.message: Then by position in the list. Every entry keeps its place, including entries written like "3" or "20".

guide_processing_order_p_3.message: Here the token is rewritten before utm_source is removed, although it comes second:

guide_processing_order_p_4.message: Rules that are off are left out. $removeparam filters and @@ entries are outside this sort and can't have an order, not even null; filters always run last.

guide_processing_order_p_5.message: Two entries with the same matchPattern text in one group are one rule. The groups are raw (rawRules), field (rules without the referral mark) and referral (marked rules objects, then referralMarketing). This mostly happens when rule lists are merged.

guide_processing_order_item_8.message: The last definition that isn't off wins, with all its keys.

guide_processing_order_item_9.message: Without its own order, the winner takes the first definition's position and the nearest earlier order. "order": null means no order, and drops an inherited one.

guide_processing_order_item_10.message: The ids and aliases of replaced definitions switch the winner on and off too.

guide_processing_order_item_11.message: While referral-marketing rules run, a referral entry replaces a field entry with the same text.

guide_processing_order_item_12.message: A raw rule and a field rule with the same text don't collide; both run.

guide_processing_order_p_6.message: Inside one list, two different entries with the same text are an error, and an exact copy is a warning.

guide_processing_order_item_13.message: At most 10 cycles run per request; at the cap the URL is used as it stands.

guide_processing_order_item_14.message: A rule with replacePattern applies at most once per request.

guide_processing_order_item_15.message: A step that doesn't change the URL doesn't start a new cycle.

guide_processing_order_p_7.message: Settings → Unbounded cleaning cycles (off by default) removes the 10-cycle cap for rule chains that need more. Processing then ends when a cycle changes nothing, but two rules that redirect to each other loop until the browser gives up and the page doesn't load. Turn it on only for rules you trust.

guide_rule_ids_p_1.message: Every rule has an id. A rule without id gets one from its list and its text: "utm_source" in rules becomes field-utm-source. A generated id changes when the rule's text changes, and a switched-off rule would then switch back on. Give a rule its own id when it must keep its on/off setting through edits, and list old ids in aliases when you rename it.

guide_rule_ids_p_2.message: A rule is switched on and off by its provider and id together, such as shop::session-token, so two providers can use the same id. The custom rules editor may also save it under the provider's pattern, such as domainPattern:||shop.example^::session-token; both forms work.

guide_rule_ids_item_1.message: Within one provider, every id and alias must be different. Generated ids count.

guide_rule_ids_item_2.message: An id can't contain a colon.

guide_rule_ids_item_3.message: A setting saved under a bare id, without its provider, switches nothing; switch the rule off again in the custom rules editor.

guide_remote_rules_p_1.message: Remote rule lists are rule files Linkumori downloads, optionally checked against a hash file. A list with an invalid cln value, defaults block or patches array is not loaded, and Remote Rules Health reports it.

guide_remote_rules_subtitle_1.message: Redirect and block need your approval

guide_remote_rules_p_2.message: What a remote list can do is worked out from its content when it loads:

guide_remote_rules_th_2.message: The list has it when it contains

guide_remote_rules_cell_1.message: a rules, rawRules or referralMarketing entry, or a $removeparam filter

guide_remote_rules_cell_3.message: a provider exceptions entry or an @@ entry

guide_remote_rules_p_3.message: Approve redirect and block per list in Remote Rules Health. Until then, that list's redirects and blocks stay off, and its raw rules can't send a URL to another site; the rest of the list works right away. When an update adds a new capability, it waits for approval too. Built-in and custom rules have every capability.

guide_remote_rules_p_4.message: Normally, remote lists that have providers replace the built-in rules; lists that hold only patches are applied to the built-in rules. With Enable Overload Mode on, they load together, using one of three strategies:

guide_remote_rules_item_1.message: Patch mode only: apply the remote lists' patches to the built-in rules; remote providers are left out.

guide_remote_rules_item_2.message: Patch mode + merge: merge built-in and remote providers, then apply patches.

guide_remote_rules_item_3.message: No patch mode + merge: merge the providers and skip patches.

guide_remote_rules_p_5.message: When merging, remote lists are merged with each other in the order you list them, then with the built-in rules (built-in first). Only providers with the same domainPatterns (or urlPattern) and the same methods, resourceTypes, completeProvider and forceRedirection merge; their rules, rawRules and referralMarketing are joined, and Same text twice decides which copy runs. Remote Rules Health lists every replaced rule as a notice.

guide_remote_rules_p_6.message: Custom rules are applied last. A custom provider replaces every loaded provider with the same pattern; their rules are not combined.

guide_remote_rules_p_7.message: A remote list can replace single rules that are already loaded, without publishing a full copy, in a top-level patches array:

guide_remote_rules_cell_7.message: Required. The rule to replace, written like its on/off key: providerKey::id, domainPattern:<pattern>::id or urlPattern:<regex>::id.

guide_remote_rules_cell_9.message: Required. The new rule, as a plain entry or a rule object.

guide_remote_rules_cell_10.message: A note for people reading the file.

guide_remote_rules_item_4.message: Patches run after remote lists are merged and before custom rules. A file with only patches needs no providers.

guide_remote_rules_item_5.message: Merging can rename providers, so the domainPattern: or urlPattern: form is the one that always finds them.

guide_remote_rules_item_6.message: The replacement keeps the old rule's id, or takes the old id as an alias, so on/off settings keep applying.

guide_remote_rules_item_7.message: A patch for a redirect waits for the list's redirect approval. A patch whose target matches nothing changes nothing.

guide_remote_rules_item_8.message: Remote Rules Health lists each patch as applied, unmatched or skipped.

guide_whitelist_p_1.message: The whitelist is separate from a provider's exceptions: it lists sites you told Linkumori to leave alone, with no rule file involved. Entries look like example.com, *.example.com (the site and its subdomains) or example.* (any suffix). Whitelisting a page also covers everything it loads.

guide_ex1_p.message: Removes tracking parameters and an affiliate id on one shop, and leaves its checkout pages alone:

guide_ex3_p.message: Sends links through a click tracker straight to their destination, which is in the url parameter:

guide_ex4_title.message: Keep a parameter on one page

guide_ex4_p.message: Removes ref everywhere on the site except on the login page, which needs it:

guide_checking_p_1.message: The custom rules editor checks rules when you save or import them, and node linkumori-cli-tool.js lint-rules <file> runs the same checks. Besides broken JSON and invalid regular expressions, they reject rules that would load but quietly do the wrong thing, such as:

guide_check_2.message: a pattern with a single | and no scheme, such as |example.com^

guide_check_3.message: a regular-expression redirect without exactly one capture group

guide_check_8.message: an id or alias used twice in one provider

guide_checking_item_2.message: two different entries with the same text in one list

guide_checking_item_3.message: an order on a $removeparam filter or @@ entry, null included

guide_check_9.message: a $redirect= address that is not http or https

guide_check_10.message: a backslash in a $removeparam name before a character that has no escape

guide_check_6.message: an @@…$rawrule= entry that stops no raw rule

guide_checking_p_2.message: They also warn about exact copies, and about the same text in both rules and referralMarketing. If saving fails, the message names the provider, the list and the entry.

customRulesEditor_syntaxRedirectEntryFor.message: $WHERE$: a redirect starting with "|" must look like "||example.com^$redirect=https://target/"

customRulesEditor_syntaxRedirectTargetNo.message: $WHERE$: the $redirect= target must be an absolute http or https URL

customRulesEditor_syntaxPreprocessorInpu.message: $WHERE$.inputs must be "all" or an array of positive integers

customRulesEditor_syntaxRuleMustBeString.message: $WHERE$ must be a string or rule object

customRulesEditor_syntaxTargetIdOnlyRawR.message: $WHERE$.targetId only applies to "@@…$rawrule=" exceptions in rawRules

customRulesEditor_syntaxFlagsNotString.message: $WHERE$.flags must be a string (regex flags such as "i")

customRulesEditor_syntaxReferralMarketin.message: $WHERE$.referralMarketing has no effect in $FIELD$; it only applies in $LISTS$

customRulesEditor_syntaxOrderNotNumber.message: $WHERE$.order must be a number or null

customRulesEditor_syntaxAliasesPattern.message: $WHERE$.aliases must be a list of ids matching $PATTERN$

customRulesEditor_syntaxAliasesContainOw.message: $WHERE$.aliases must not contain the rule's own id

customRulesEditor_syntaxExceptionsNotStr.message: $WHERE$.exceptions must be an array of strings

customRulesEditor_syntaxRequestTypesNotS.message: $WHERE$.requestTypes must be an array of strings

customRulesEditor_syntaxFieldRedirection.message: $WHERE$ starts with "@@", which only applies to $removeparam filters in rules and referralMarketing; use a rule object's "exceptions" instead

customRulesEditor_syntaxSinglePipe.message: $WHERE$: "$PATTERN$" starts with a single "|", so it only matches URLs that literally begin with "$REST$" and none do (URLs start with "https://"). Use "||$REST$" to match the domain.

customRulesEditor_syntaxTargetIdNeedsExc.message: $WHERE$ has "targetId", which only works on an exception; start matchPattern with "@@" (e.g. "@@||example.com^$rawrule=")

customRulesEditor_syntaxTargetIdAndRegex.message: $WHERE$ has both "targetId" and a regex after "rawrule="; use one of them

customRulesEditor_syntaxTargetIdUnknown.message: $WHERE$ has targetId "$ID$", but no raw rule in this provider has that id or alias

customRulesEditor_syntaxExceptionRegexUn.message: $WHERE$ is an "@@" exception for "$REGEX$", but no raw rule in this provider uses that regex. Give the rule an id and point at it with "targetId" instead

customRulesEditor_syntaxExceptionKeyNoEf.message: $WHERE$ is an "@@" exception, so "$KEY$" would do nothing

customRulesEditor_syntaxRawRuleMissingRe.message: $WHERE$ has nothing after "rawrule="; it needs the regex to delete

customRulesEditor_syntaxRedirectCaptureG.message: $WHERE$ has $GROUPS$ capture groups; it needs exactly one "( … )" around the destination URL (write other groups as "(?: … )")

customRulesEditor_syntaxRuleIdReused.message: $PROVIDER$ reuses rule id "$ID$" in $WHERE$; first used in $FIRST$
